failures: src/contextlens/agents/single.py _numbers / _numbers_supported (lines 164-193): the number rule can be fooled into keeping a wrong number when the quote spells a compound number. _WORDS maps each word alone, so 'twenty-five' yields {20, 5}, and 'five hundred' / 'five thousand' yields {5}. Reproduce: single._numbers_supported on a Finding with statement '5 dollars' and quote 'five hundred dollars' returns True; statement '20 dollars' vs 'twenty-five dollars' returns True. Spelled-out scale words are common in speech transcripts, so a misread amount (5 for 5,000) passes. Also, number words in the statement are never checked (words=False): statement 'five dollars' vs quote 'fifty dollars', or 'three dollars' vs '$13', is kept. The docstring lists non-matching cases but not these. Fix idea: treat a number word adjacent to hundred/thousand/million/-teens/tens compounds (hyphenated or followed by a scale word) as unmatched, and parse small number words in the statement too; add tests for these.
notes: Everything else in the Decision holds. Known limit, not a failure: a kept finding that repeats an injected claim can reach the second call's suggestion. A respond card whose suggestion failed stays 'answered' with findings (acceptable, flagged in missing). The 'no verified findings' note can appear when the model's mode was respond but the guard abstained the card (mode then shows recall); cosmetic. _ABANDONED is a module-level list mutated from several threads without a lock; benign in CPython. The pytest rootdir for files under the main folder imports the main folder's src despite PYTHONPATH, so I used -c pyproject.toml --rootdir=<worktree> and a Windows-style PYTHONPATH. test_no_raw_text was not counted per instructions.
